questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In E.P. Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu, arbitrariness was described as:

options.C: A matter only for the legislature to decide

questions.explanation: Royappa gave the dynamic, anti-arbitrariness dimension to Article 14.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Article 15(3) permits the State to make special provisions for:

options.D: Only Scheduled Tribes in the States

questions.explanation: Article 15(3) is an exception to the bar on discrimination on the ground of sex.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Reservation in promotions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes was enabled by Article 16(4A), inserted by the:
questions.explanation: The amendment overcame the effect of Indra Sawhney, which had barred reservation in promotions.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The right to emergency medical treatment was read into Article 21 in:

options.A: Paschim Banga Khet Mazdoor Samity v. W.B. (1996)
options.B: Francis Coralie Mullin v. Administrator, Delhi (1981)
options.C: Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992)
options.D: Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993)

questions.explanation: The Court held that failure to provide timely medical treatment to a person in need violates the right to life.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala, students who refused to sing the national anthem were held to be protected under:
questions.explanation: Standing respectfully without singing was held to be a protected form of silent expression and religious conviction.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Article 28(1) prohibits religious instruction in educational institutions:

options.C: Wholly maintained out of State funds

questions.explanation: Institutions administered by trusts but recognised by the State may provide religious instruction voluntarily under Article 28(2) and (3).

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: 'Equal pay for equal work' was held enforceable through Articles 14 and 16 read with Article 39(d) in:

options.A: Randhir Singh v. Union of India
options.B: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab

questions.explanation: The Court made a Directive Principle enforceable by reading it into the Fundamental Rights.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Article 48A, inserted by the 42nd Amendment, directs the State to protect and improve:
questions.explanation: Article 51A(g) casts a corresponding Fundamental Duty on citizens.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In the election of the President, the electoral college does NOT include:

options.A: Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies
options.B: Elected members of the Rajya Sabha
options.D: Elected members of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 54, nominated members and members of Legislative Councils do not vote.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Under Article 85, the gap between two sessions of Parliament must not exceed:
questions.explanation: Parliament must meet at least twice a year.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Under Article 100, the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is:

options.A: One-fourth of the total number of members
options.B: One-half of the total number of members
options.C: One-third of the total number of members
options.D: One-tenth of the total number of members

questions.explanation: The quorum includes the presiding officer.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: A State Legislative Council may be created or abolished by Parliament on a resolution of the Legislative Assembly passed by:

options.A: A simple majority of the Assembly
options.B: A two-thirds majority of the Council
options.D: A special majority of the Assembly

questions.explanation: Article 169 requires a majority of the total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting; this is not a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The Attorney General of India holds office:

options.A: During the pleasure of the President
options.B: For a fixed term of five years

questions.explanation: Article 76 contains no fixed term or procedure for removal.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Karl Llewellyn is a leading figure of:
questions.explanation: Llewellyn's The Bramble Bush advanced the realist emphasis on what courts do.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The Critical Legal Studies movement is associated with:
questions.explanation: CLS argues that law is indeterminate and reflects power relations.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Feminist jurisprudence, criticising law as reflecting male power, is associated with:
questions.explanation: MacKinnon argued that the State is male in the feminist sense.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: In Marxist theory, law is regarded as:

options.A: An independent force shaping the economy
options.C: A neutral expression of reason alone
options.D: Part of the superstructure of the economy

questions.explanation: The economic base determines the legal and political superstructure.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The 'harm principle', that State power over an individual is justified only to prevent harm to others, is associated with:
questions.explanation: Mill set out the principle in On Liberty (1859).

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: In the 'will theory' of rights, a right is essentially:

options.A: A choice or control given to the right-holder
options.C: A benefit conferred by law on the right-holder
options.D: A moral claim without legal force

questions.explanation: Hart favoured the will theory, while Raz favoured the interest theory.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Penal liability arises where the purpose of the law is to:
questions.explanation: Remedial liability, in contrast, aims at redress or restitution.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: A 'del credere' agent, for an extra commission, undertakes:

options.A: To guarantee payment by the buyers
options.B: To deliver goods free of all taxes
options.C: To store goods without any charge
options.D: To sell goods only at a fixed price

questions.explanation: He becomes a surety to the principal for the buyer's payment.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Agency by estoppel arises where the principal:

options.A: Holds out another as his agent

questions.explanation: The principal is estopped from denying the agent's authority against persons who relied on the representation.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 39 of the Contract Act, when a party refuses to perform his promise in its entirety, the other party may:

options.C: Put an end to the contract
options.D: Transfer the contract to a third person

questions.explanation: The innocent party may also elect to continue the contract.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 55 of the Contract Act, if time is of the essence and the promisor fails to perform in time, the contract is:
questions.explanation: The promisee can treat the contract as terminated.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 69 of the Indian Partnership Act, an unregistered firm cannot:

options.A: Carry on any business or profession at all
options.B: Sue third parties on its contracts
options.C: Be sued by third parties on its contracts
options.D: Hold property in the partners' names

questions.explanation: The bar does not affect suits for dissolution or rights arising otherwise than from contract.

questions.subject: Sale of Goods
questions.question: An unpaid seller in possession of the goods may exercise the right of:
questions.explanation: Other rights include stoppage in transit and resale in certain cases.

questions.subject: Sale of Goods
questions.question: Under Section 18 of the Sale of Goods Act, in a contract for sale of unascertained goods, property does not pass until the goods are:
questions.explanation: Ascertainment makes the goods identifiable and specific.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: State of Rajasthan v. Vidhyawati held that the State is:

options.A: Immune for every tort of its servants and agents
options.B: Liable only for torts of ministers
options.C: Vicariously liable like any other employer

questions.explanation: The Court held that the State is liable for a driver's negligence in a non-sovereign function.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: The 'rescue doctrine' in negligence holds that a rescuer injured in a rescue:

options.A: Can sue the person who created the danger
options.B: Can sue only the person rescued
options.C: Has no remedy at all if he is a stranger
options.D: Is barred by the maxim volenti non fit injuria

questions.explanation: Haynes v. Harwood held that rescuers are not deemed to consent to the risk.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Re Polemis held a defendant liable for all direct consequences of his negligent act, whether or not they were:
questions.explanation: The Wagon Mound (No. 1) later replaced this test with reasonable foreseeability.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: The defence of fair comment in defamation applies to:

options.A: Any purely private matter between individuals
options.B: Honest opinion on public interest matters
options.D: A false statement of fact made carelessly

questions.explanation: The comment must be based on true facts and be made without malice.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Slander is actionable per se, without proof of special damage, when it imputes:
questions.explanation: Other slander per se categories include loathsome disease, unchastity of a woman and professional incompetence.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Abatement of a nuisance means:

options.B: Removal of nuisance by the injured party
options.C: Payment of damages by the wrongdoer
options.D: Transfer of the property to the plaintiff

questions.explanation: It is a remedy by self-help, exercised without unnecessary damage and after notice, where required.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Kidnapping is defined in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 137 corresponds to Sections 359 to 363 IPC.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Criminal intimidation is dealt with in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 351 corresponds to Section 503 IPC.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Criminal trespass is defined in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 329 corresponds to Section 441 IPC.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Forgery is defined in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 336 corresponds to Section 463 IPC; Section 335 defines making a false document.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: In Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab, the Supreme Court explained that murder is made out where the intended injury was:

options.A: Caused by a deadly weapon, in every single case
options.C: Sufficient to cause death in ordinary course
options.D: Likely to cause hurt in some cases

questions.explanation: Virsa Singh applies the third clause of murder, where the injury is objectively sufficient to cause death.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt is punishable under which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 117 corresponds to Section 325 IPC.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Gang rape is punishable under which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 70 corresponds to Section 376D IPC.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: The right of private defence of property extends to voluntarily causing death where the offence is:
questions.explanation: The right extends to causing death only in specified serious offences such as robbery, house-breaking by night, arson and theft or mischief creating reasonable fear of death.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Section 478 of the BNSS, in a bailable offence, bail is granted:

options.D: Only after one month in custody

questions.explanation: Section 478 corresponds to Section 436 CrPC.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Maintenance of wives, children and parents under the BNSS is provided in Section:
questions.explanation: Section 144 BNSS corresponds to Section 125 CrPC.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: The inherent powers of the High Court under the BNSS are saved in Section:
questions.explanation: Section 528 BNSS corresponds to Section 482 CrPC; Section 482 BNSS now deals with anticipatory bail.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Section 356 of the BNSS provides for trial in the absence of:
questions.explanation: The provision enables trial where the accused has absconded and been declared a proclaimed offender, subject to safeguards.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: A Chief Judicial Magistrate can ordinarily pass a sentence of imprisonment up to:
questions.explanation: A Magistrate of the First Class can pass up to three years.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: A death sentence passed by a Sessions Court must be confirmed by:
questions.explanation: Confirmation proceedings are conducted under the Code of Criminal Procedure (BNSS).

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: A 'charge' in a criminal trial is:

options.A: A formal statement of the offence alleged
options.B: The report filed by the police station
options.C: The order granting bail to the accused
options.D: A summons issued to the witnesses

questions.explanation: The charge informs the accused of the offence and the particulars needed to defend.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: A police officer can arrest without a warrant in a:
questions.explanation: A non-cognizable offence ordinarily requires a magistrate's order or warrant.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Leading questions may be put without the court's permission in:
questions.explanation: Section 143 of the Evidence Act allows leading questions in cross-examination.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 126 of the Evidence Act, an advocate cannot disclose, without the client's consent:

options.A: The names of other clients of the advocate
options.C: The fees charged to the client for advice

questions.explanation: The privilege continues even after the engagement ends.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: A child of tender years is a competent witness if he:

options.A: Has been trained by a lawyer before the trial
options.B: Is above twelve years of age
options.C: Is accompanied by a parent or guardian in court
options.D: Can understand questions and answer rationally

questions.explanation: Section 118 makes all persons competent unless prevented from understanding questions or giving rational answers.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 122 of the Evidence Act, communications between spouses during marriage are:
questions.explanation: Disclosure is allowed in suits between married persons and prosecutions of one against the other.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The concept of obligations erga omnes was articulated by the ICJ in:
questions.explanation: The Court distinguished obligations owed to the international community as a whole.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Genocide, under the 1948 Convention, requires intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a:

options.C: National, ethnical, racial or religious group

questions.explanation: Political groups are not protected under the Convention's definition.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The rule of speciality in extradition means that the person may be tried only for:

options.B: The offence for which he was extradited
options.D: Any offence in the requesting State

questions.explanation: It protects the surrendered person from trial for other offences without the consent of the surrendering State.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The Kellogg–Briand Pact, 1928 was an agreement to:
questions.explanation: It was signed in Paris and influenced later prohibition of aggressive war.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Under Article 36(2) of the ICJ Statute, States may accept the Court's compulsory jurisdiction through the:
questions.explanation: India has made a declaration under the optional clause with several reservations.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: In Nicaragua v. United States (1986), the ICJ held that the principle of non-use of force was:
questions.explanation: The Court held that customary law continues independently of treaty law.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: Under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the property of a Hindu male dying intestate devolves first on:
questions.explanation: Class I heirs include sons, daughters, widow and mother, among others.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: Property of a Hindu female dying intestate, not inherited from her parents or husband's family, devolves first on:
questions.explanation: Section 15(1)(a) HSA lists sons, daughters (including children of pre-deceased children) and husband together.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: Under Sunni law, a widow with children is entitled to what share in her husband's estate?
questions.explanation: Without children, her share is one-fourth.

questions.subject: Succession Law
questions.question: Under Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, a will must be attested by:

options.B: A notary public with a seal
options.C: A magistrate of the first class
options.D: One witness of the testator's choice

questions.explanation: Each witness must see the testator sign or acknowledge his signature.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: The right of pre-emption (shufa) in Muslim law is the right to:

options.D: Buy property before a stranger can

questions.explanation: It is based on the notion of avoiding the inconvenience of a stranger as co-sharer or neighbour.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: A waqf is the permanent dedication of property for:

options.D: Private enjoyment of the founder's heirs only

questions.explanation: The ownership of waqf property is vested in God, and a mutawalli manages it.

questions.subject: Information Technology Law
questions.question: Identity theft is punishable under which section of the IT Act, 2000?
questions.explanation: Section 66F deals with cyber terrorism and Section 66A was struck down in Shreya Singhal.

questions.subject: Labour & Women Law
questions.question: Under the POSH Act, 2013, an Internal Committee must be constituted at every workplace with at least:
questions.explanation: Establishments with fewer than ten employees fall under the Local Committee at the district level.

questions.subject: Insolvency Law
questions.question: Under the IBC, 2016, the minimum default amount for initiating corporate insolvency (since 2020) is:
questions.explanation: The threshold was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹1 crore in March 2020.

questions.subject: Environmental Law
questions.question: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognises the rights of:

options.D: Forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers

questions.explanation: The Act recognises individual and community forest rights.

questions.subject: Environmental Law
questions.question: The National Biodiversity Authority is established under the:
questions.explanation: The Act implements the Convention on Biological Diversity, 1992.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Under RERA, 2016, registration of a real estate project is required where the land exceeds:
questions.explanation: Section 3 of the Act sets this threshold.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Under the LARR Act, 2013, acquisition for private companies requires the consent of at least:

options.A: 67 per cent of the affected families
options.B: 80 per cent of the affected families
options.C: 100 per cent of the affected families
options.D: 51 per cent of the affected families

questions.explanation: For public-private partnership projects the consent threshold is 70 per cent.

questions.subject: Company Law
questions.question: Under Section 188 of the Companies Act, 2013, related party transactions require:

options.A: Approval of the Registrar of Companies only
options.C: Approval of the Tribunal alone in every case
options.D: Board approval, and shareholders' above limits

questions.explanation: Interested directors and members cannot vote on the related party resolution.

questions.subject: Right to Information
questions.question: The Central Information Commission under the RTI Act is headed by the:
questions.explanation: The Commission hears second appeals and complaints under the Act.

questions.subject: Securities Law
questions.question: Insider trading in India is prohibited under the:

options.D: Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and its rules

questions.explanation: The SEBI Act, 1992 empowers SEBI to regulate and penalise insider trading.
